title: Nine Months on Nasdaq: Why Pets.com Chose an Orderly Wind-Down
conflicts: Closing share price 19 cents in afternoon trade (CNN) vs 22-cent close (AP/CBS, Pinsent Masons): close used. Wainwright's own accounts of the divorce differ (that morning, HerMoney; the day before, SmartCompany): story says 'that same week'. HerMoney says she was picked to run Pets.com in early 2000, contradicted by Newsweek (June 1999) and CNET (Feb 2000): not used. Amazon stake 24.5% to 50% depending on date: no figure given. Shareholder payout: only the company's own estimate of up to about $0.25 a share is used; the circulating '17 cents' figure is unsourced and omitted.
notes: Founder field set honestly to 'Greg McLemore (founder); Julie Wainwright (chief executive)', and the story says plainly the business was not her idea. The executive retention bonuses (Computerworld, from the 10-Q) are included factually, with analysts' doubts attributed to them. The repeat screen flagged Quibi and Souq as 'same-founder' (probably the shared '(founder)'/'(chief executive)' wording) but let it through. Stance affirms (Crito 44c).
